newsitem.title: USA: Prudential urges judge to approve settlement.
newsitem.headline: Prudential urges judge to approve settlement.

text.p: Prudential Insurance Co of America urged a federal judge Monday to approve its proposed class action settlement of deceptive sales practice complaints, saying policy holders who were misled will be fully compensated under the plan.

In a hearing before U.S. District Judge Alfred Wolin, Prudential called the settlement "extraordinary" because it offers 100 percent compensation to policy holders who were misled by the company's agents.
Under the plan, which now has the backing of every state insurance regulator, Prudential also is waiving its right to several key defenses such as the statute of limitations.
The settlement is "fair and adequate and supported by every regulator in the country," Prudential attorney Reid Ashinoff said.
The proposed settlement also won support from the lead attorney representing the plaintiffs in the class action case.
The settlement offers swift and efficient relief to policy holders who were wronged, attorney Mel Weiss said.
